title: A Comprehensive Research Report on Asian Mythologies

traditions.creation: The myth of Pangu describes a giant emerging from a cosmic egg to separate yin and yang. Nüwa is credited with creating humans from clay and repairing the sky.
traditions.pantheon: Led by the Jade Emperor (Yu Huang), acting as a celestial bureaucracy.

traditions.creation: Izanagi and Izanami gave birth to the islands of Japan; their separation established the boundaries of life and death.
traditions.deities: Amaterasu (Sun Goddess), Susanoo (Storm God), and Tsukuyomi (Moon God).

traditions.cosmology: Cyclical time (yugas) involving endless creation, preservation, and dissolution.

traditions.narratives: The life of Siddhartha Gautama and the Jataka tales (previous lives of the Buddha).

traditions.creation: The Enuma Elish depicts Marduk's victory over the primordial chaos monster Tiamat.
traditions.narrative: The Epic of Gilgamesh explores the quest for immortality and the acceptance of human mortality.

traditions.dualism: The struggle between Ahura Mazda (Good) and Angra Mainyu (Evil).
traditions.legacy: Influenced concepts of monotheism and final judgment in later religions.
